pr.title: Feature flag: rolling-updates

raw_findings.body: The rendered command either duplicates the `--features` option (CLI rejects/overwrites it) or, when copied literally, generates metadata with only `rolling-updates` enabled, so the recorded feature set does not match the real deployment and the compatibility verdict is wrong.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documented command is not copy-pasteable for real deployments and produces misleading compatibility metadata.
raw_findings.impact: The rendered command either duplicates the `--features` option (CLI rejects/overwrites it) or, when copied literally, generates metadata with only `rolling-updates` enabled, so the recorded feature set does not match the real deployment and the compatibility verdict is wrong.
raw_findings.root_cause: A deployment-specific preview feature flag was baked into a generic FreeMarker macro used by every documented invocation instead of being part of the per-invocation parameters.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the hardcoded flag from the shared `updatecompatibility` macro and instead document in the guide that `rolling-updates` must be appended to the user's existing `--features` list (e.g. add it to the `parameters` of each invocation with an explanatory note).
raw_findings.title: Doc macro hardcodes `--features=rolling-updates`, conflicting with the user's own `--features` value
raw_findings.trigger: A user follows update-compatibility.adoc, which explicitly requires passing *all* configuration options (including their own `--features=...` list) to `metadata`/`check`; the rendered command already appends a second `--features=rolling-updates`.

raw_findings.body: The CLI keeps telling users to enable a feature name that no longer exists, and the hardcoded literal silently diverges from `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()` used by the callers' guard, so the error message no longer matches the checked feature.
raw_findings.evidence: printError("Unable to use this command. The preview feature 'rolling-updates' is not enabled.");
raw_findings.failure_mode: Message and guard can drift apart during future refactors, misleading operators.
raw_findings.impact: The CLI keeps telling users to enable a feature name that no longer exists, and the hardcoded literal silently diverges from `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()` used by the callers' guard, so the error message no longer matches the checked feature.
raw_findings.root_cause: New helper introduces a magic string duplicating the feature key that is already available as a constant from the `Profile.Feature` enum.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Build the message from `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()` (e.g. `"... The preview feature '%s' is not enabled.".formatted(Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey())`) instead of the literal `rolling-updates`.
raw_findings.title: Feature key duplicated as a string literal in `printFeatureDisabled`
raw_findings.trigger: The `ROLLING_UPDATES` enum label/key in `Profile.Feature` is renamed or the feature is graduated/removed in a later release.

raw_findings.body: The constant name does not convey that it is a process exit code (unlike its two sibling constants in the same interface), making it easy to confuse with a result state and to misuse in comparisons of `CompatibilityResult#exitCode()`.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent API naming in a public interface reduces readability and invites misuse.
raw_findings.impact: The constant name does not convey that it is a process exit code (unlike its two sibling constants in the same interface), making it easy to confuse with a result state and to misuse in comparisons of `CompatibilityResult#exitCode()`.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new sibling constant was added to the exit-code group without following the established `*_EXIT_CODE` suffix used by the adjacent declarations.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the constant to `FEATURE_DISABLED_EXIT_CODE` (and update the two `picocli.exit(...)` call sites) to match the existing `*_EXIT_CODE` convention.
raw_findings.title: New exit-code constant `FEATURE_DISABLED` breaks the `_EXIT_CODE` naming convention of the interface
raw_findings.trigger: Any developer reading/using `CompatibilityResult` alongside `ROLLING_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` and `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE`, e.g. at the call site `picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED)`.

raw_findings.body: The statement is unverifiable against the code: the Operator contains no `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` check (only the server CLI commands check it), so the Operator keeps reconciling normally and the documented failure never occurs, misleading users about the actual requirement.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale/incorrect documentation describes behavior the shipped code does not exhibit.
raw_findings.impact: The statement is unverifiable against the code: the Operator contains no `Profile.isFeatureEnabled` check (only the server CLI commands check it), so the Operator keeps reconciling normally and the documented failure never occurs, misleading users about the actual requirement.
raw_findings.root_cause: Documentation was written for an enforcement behavior that the patch does not implement in the operator module.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Reword the caution to state precisely what fails (the server-side `update-compatibility` commands exit with code 4 when the feature is disabled) and that the flag must be enabled on the Keycloak server via `spec.features.enabled`, or add the corresponding validation in the Operator.
raw_findings.title: Operator guide claims the Operator fails without `rolling-updates`, but no such check exists
raw_findings.trigger: A user deploys a Keycloak CR with `spec.update.strategy` set but without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature and expects the Operator to fail as documented.

raw_findings.body: Previously enabled features of the base test deployment are silently discarded, so the deployed server runs with a feature set different from the one other tests rely on, potentially masking or causing spurious failures.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test fixture silently loses configuration, weakening the validity of the upgrade assertions.
raw_findings.impact: Previously enabled features of the base test deployment are silently discarded, so the deployed server runs with a feature set different from the one other tests rely on, potentially masking or causing spurious failures.
raw_findings.root_cause: The setter unconditionally replaces the enabled-features collection although the surrounding code assumes a FeatureSpec may already be populated.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Append to the existing list instead of replacing it, e.g. build a new list from `getEnabledFeatures()` (when non-null) plus `Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES.getKey()`.
raw_findings.title: UpgradeTest overwrites any pre-existing enabled features in the test CR
raw_findings.trigger: `getTestKeycloakDeployment(true)` returns a CR whose `spec.features.enabled` already contains entries (the preceding null-check on `getFeatureSpec()` exists precisely because the spec can be non-null).

raw_findings.body: The scriptable contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc (exit code 3 = recreate required, 4 = feature disabled) is unverified, so a future accidental change of these constants would break user automation without any test failing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Regression in the documented exit-code contract would pass CI undetected.
raw_findings.impact: The scriptable contract documented in update-compatibility.adoc (exit code 3 = recreate required, 4 = feature disabled) is unverified, so a future accidental change of these constants would break user automation without any test failing.
raw_findings.root_cause: Exit-code constants were redefined as part of a documented CLI contract without adding assertions covering their values.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend `UpdateCommandDistTest` to assert `assertEquals(3, result.exitCode())` for the incompatible case and `assertEquals(4, ...)` for the feature-disabled case.
raw_findings.title: Changed recreate exit code (4 -> 3) is not asserted by any test
raw_findings.trigger: Running `UpdateCommandDistTest.testWrongVersions`, the only test exercising an incompatible configuration; it asserts only the error message and never inspects `result.exitCode()`.

validated_findings.title: Changed recreate exit code (4 -> 3) is not asserted by any test
validated_findings.trigger: Running `UpdateCommandDistTest.testWrongVersions`, the only test exercising an incompatible configuration; it asserts only the error message and never inspects `result.exitCode()`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about missing exit code assertions is a test coverage suggestion, not a defect in the patch. The exit codes are documented in update-compatibility.adoc and the code correctly implements them. The test `testWrongVersions` uses `assertError` which validates behavior. Missing assertions for specific exit codes is a test gap observation, not a bug introduced by this patch.
